{"id": "ec4f0d3f-2f7a-4e17-b2ac-e8a94c43d5de", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "EKS managed node groups and Fargate profiles are two different ways to run your pods' compute in EKS — the big difference is **EC2-based vs serverless**.

**Managed Node Groups**
- Backed by EC2 instances that AWS provisions and lifecycles for you (via an Auto Scaling Group)
- You choose instance types, AMI, disk size, and can use Spot or On-Demand
- AWS automates provisioning, updates, and graceful termination/draining during upgrades
- You still manage capacity (scaling, right-sizing) and pay for the underlying EC2 instances whether or not they're fully utilized
- Supports DaemonSets, privileged containers, GPU workloads, and most Kubernetes features without restriction
- Good for: steady-state workloads, GPU/specialized instance needs, workloads needing full node-level control

**Fargate Profiles**
- Serverless — no EC2 instances to manage at all; AWS runs each pod in its own isolated micro-VM
- You define profiles matching namespace + label selectors; pods matching those criteria get scheduled on Fargate automatically
- You pay per-pod for vCPU/memory requested, not for idle node capacity
- Each pod gets its own kernel/isolation boundary (stronger multi-tenancy isolation)
- Limitations: no DaemonSets, no privileged containers, no GPU support, no hostPort/hostNetwork, limited to certain storage options (no EBS, only EFS for persistent volumes), and pod sizes are capped at fixed vCPU/memory combinations
- Good for: bursty or unpredictable workloads, multi-tenant isolation needs, teams that don't want to manage node capacity at all

Quick rule of thumb: if you need fine-grained control, DaemonSets, GPUs, or cost efficiency at steady high utilization — go with managed node groups. If you want zero infrastructure management and are fine with the per-pod pricing and feature restrictions, Fargate profiles are simpler.

Let me know if you'd like to see which approach your current EKS clusters are using.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
